tagline.text: A small resort island and marine sanctuary on the reef off Cordova

location.label: Location
location.text: Off Gilutongan barangay, Cordova, Cebu (Olango Island Group)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–3,500 (per person, including entrance fee, gear and meals; boat cost shared among the group)

children.text: Nalusuan is a small island of about one hectare in Cordova, east of Mactan Island, and the whole island is a resort and marine sanctuary. It is roughly 30 minutes by boat from Mactan, and its boardwalk over the shallow reef and its snorkeling have made it a popular island-hopping stop.

Nalusuan Island is a small island of the Olango Island Group in the Cebu Strait, between mainland Cebu and Bohol. Administratively it belongs to Gilutongan barangay in the municipality of Cordova, and Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap point to the same location (about 10.19° N, 124.00° E). It covers a little under one hectare, so walking around it takes only a few minutes.

The island is known to have been built on a sandbar that was reclaimed for a resort. The Philippine Star (2014) also described it as an artificial resort island off Mactan, and the entire island is occupied by the Nalusuan Island Resort and Marine Sanctuary. So instead of expecting an untouched desert island, think of it as a small, tidy marine park built on top of a reef. A story says local fishermen named it for the sea cucumbers in the surrounding waters, but this is not confirmed in the literature.

The sea around Nalusuan is managed as a marine sanctuary. The reefs here were once badly damaged by dynamite fishing and overfishing, but fish are reported to have returned as the sanctuary was declared and patrolled. The nearby Gilutongan (Hilutungan) sanctuary was established by an ordinance in 1999, and the municipality of Cordova has promoted both sanctuaries as tourist attractions. When you snorkel, you can see tropical fish coming close in the shallow reef along the edge of the island.

Nalusuan became famous among travelers for its long wooden boardwalk over the shallow reef and its pier-like structures. It is a great place for photos that look like walking on water, and group members who are weak swimmers and children can watch the fish from the edge. However, because the island is small and inside a resort, entrance fees and how things work depend on current operations. Island-hopping tours from Mactan often combine it with other islands such as Gilutongan and Caohagan, and you can also rent a boat to visit only Nalusuan. Either way, a stay of about an hour and a half to two hours at one stop is typical.

A long wooden boardwalk stretching over the shallow reef from the edge of the island is the symbol of this island. It is a favorite photo spot on hopping tours because you can take pictures of yourself walking above clear water. Fish are sometimes visible below the railing, so walk slowly. A waterproof case lowers the risk of dropping your phone in the water.

Because it is a sanctuary, plenty of tropical fish can be seen even close to the island. Guides describe many fish near the pier, and beginners can enjoy the shallows in a life jacket. Do not step on or touch the coral, and stay inside the designated snorkeling area.
Fish crackers are said to be sold on the island. Feeding fish human food such as bread is reportedly prohibited, so use only what is sold on the island and follow staff instructions.

The waters around Nalusuan are known as a place where both beginners and experienced divers can dive. One guide says soft and hard corals can be seen at depths of 25–40 m. People without a license can join a discovery dive; confirm gear and instructor fees with the operator.

Guides mention water activities such as kayaks, paddle boats, banana boats, jet skis and parasailing. Prices in a 2020 guide were set separately by number of people and by the hour, so confirm current prices on site. They may not operate on days with high waves.

The island has a restaurant, and a floating restaurant popular with foreign visitors is described. However, some guides say outside food is not allowed while others say some people bring things like pork barbecue, so the information conflicts. Be sure to ask about bringing food when you book.

blocks.title: The island resort and an overnight stay

children.text: The island has a resort with rooms where you can stay overnight. Booking sites list check-in at 14:00 and check-out at 12:00. One guide says electricity is supplied by a generator and is available only from 6:00 pm to 8:00 am, so ask about power and air-conditioning hours before staying.

blocks.title: The small island and its white-sand beach

children.text: There is a white-sand beach around the island, but one guide says the water is too shallow for swimming or snorkeling there. Treat the beach as a place to rest and take photos, and do your water play in the sanctuary's designated area.

One guide also says you can book a round-trip transfer to the island resort. A 2020 guide listed ₱2,500 for 1–10 people and ₱4,000 for 11–25 people, so confirm current rates and booking methods with the resort.
Nalusuan tour packages with hotel pickup and lunch are listed on travel booking sites. Be sure to check whether the entrance fee is included.
People who find a boat directly from a Mactan hotel usually split the cost of one boat among 5–10 people.
From Cebu City you can reach Cordova on the CCLEX (Cebu–Cordova Link Expressway). Check the latest toll and traffic information.
Around the Cordova wharf, get around by tricycle.
The best time for snorkeling and hopping is said to be March–June, when the sea is calm and clear. December–February and July are also fine, but there may be windy days.
August–November is strongly affected by rain and typhoons, so boats may be cancelled. Check the weather and wharf operation notices before departure.
On weekends the boardwalk is crowded with people taking photos, so weekday mornings are quieter.

Nalusuan Island is itself a resort, so staying a night is an option. The rooms are described as 2-star with air conditioning and a private bathroom, and because power on the island comes from a generator, there may be daytime hours without electricity. Prices are listed on booking sites at an average of about $84–99 per night, so check by date. Most travelers stay at a resort on Mactan Island and visit on a day tour. From a Mactan hotel to the wharf is 10–30 minutes by Grab.

For meals, use the island restaurant and floating restaurant, or choose a hopping tour that includes lunch. Rules on bringing food differ between guides, so it is safest to check when you book. Bring water and snacks to drink on the boat.
Entrance fees differ by guide from ₱150 to ₱400 and often must be paid in cash on site, so bring plenty of small bills.
Before departure, confirm the total boat price, how long you will stay, and whether the entrance fee and gear are included, by text or messenger.
Use a waterproof case for boardwalk photos, and wear reef-safe sunscreen.
We recommend a weekday morning. Weekends are crowded.
Because many tours visit two or three islands in a day, focus your time at Nalusuan on snorkeling and photos.
One guide recommends booking the resort a week ahead. A same-day visit may find it fully booked.
Use only fish food sold on the island, and do not give bread.
If the sea looks uncertain, do not force it; adjust your schedule.
On days with a flight, leave at least three hours of margin for your return.
Boats can be cancelled depending on sea conditions and typhoon forecasts, so check the weather and operation notices on the day of departure.
Do not step on, touch or collect coral, and follow the designated snorkeling area and life jacket rules.
Free diving is said to be not recommended for beginners because of strong currents.
Entrance, boat and activity prices differ greatly between guides, so be sure to confirm the total on site.
One guide says the shallow water makes swimming from the beach difficult, so do not expect to swim at the beach.
Small boats have passenger limits, so avoid boarding beyond capacity.
